subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In a stratified sample, the sampling fraction is
options: the population size divided by the sample size
the sample size divided by the population size
questions.explain: The sampling fraction equals sample size divided by population size and is applied to each stratum.

questions.q: For testing whether matches ignite, a census is unsuitable mainly because
options: the testing destroys each item tested
questions.explain: Testing every match destroys it, so a census would leave none to sell, making a sample necessary.

questions.q: To take a systematic sample of 50 from a population of 1000, you select every
questions.explain: The interval is 1000 divided by 50, which equals 20, so every 20th member is chosen.

questions.q: A factory line is sampled by taking every 100th item produced. This is an example of
questions.explain: Selecting items at a fixed regular interval is systematic sampling.

questions.q: Why might stratified sampling be impossible to carry out?
options: The strata and their sizes are unknown
questions.explain: Stratified sampling requires knowing the subgroups and their sizes; without that it cannot be applied.

questions.q: Which is a key advantage of taking a sample rather than a census?
options: It always gives results with no error
It guarantees the whole population is represented exactly
It removes all forms of bias automatically
It is generally cheaper and quicker than a census
questions.explain: Sampling is cheaper and faster than surveying an entire population, though it introduces sampling error.

questions.q: Cluster sampling involves
options: dividing the population into clusters and sampling whole selected clusters
questions.explain: In cluster sampling the population is split into clusters, some clusters are chosen, and members within them are surveyed.

questions.q: A sampling unit is
options: an individual member of the population that can be sampled
questions.explain: A sampling unit is one individual or item of the population that may be selected.

questions.q: An advantage of opportunity sampling is that it is
options: based on a full sampling frame
quick, easy and cheap to carry out
questions.explain: Opportunity sampling's main merit is speed, ease and low cost, despite its bias.

questions.q: A population is defined as
options: the whole set of items or individuals of interest
the part of the group actually surveyed
the list used to draw a sample
questions.explain: The population is the entire collection of individuals or items under investigation.

questions.q: A researcher surveys only people leaving a gym about exercise habits. The main problem is
options: selection bias toward more active people
the sample is a full census
questions.explain: Only gym-goers are reached, biasing the sample toward physically active people.

questions.q: A manager numbers all 200 staff and uses random numbers to pick 20. This is
questions.explain: Numbering the population and selecting with random numbers is simple random sampling.

questions.q: Which is generally true of a census compared with a sample?
options: It gives a fully accurate picture of the whole population but is costly and time-consuming
It is cheaper to carry out
questions.explain: A census covers the whole population accurately but is expensive and slow to conduct.

questions.q: An advantage of stratified sampling over simple random sampling is that it
options: ensures each subgroup is represented in proportion
is the only method that removes all bias
questions.explain: Stratified sampling guarantees each stratum appears in proportion to its size, improving representativeness.

questions.q: The large data set used in A-level statistics is best described as
options: a real collection of UK (and overseas) weather data students explore
a single small table of ten readings
a fictional dataset invented for exams
questions.explain: The large data set is a substantial collection of real weather-station data used to develop statistical familiarity.

questions.q: Which is NOT a random sampling method?
questions.explain: Opportunity sampling is non-random because members are chosen for convenience, not by chance.

questions.q: Bias in a sample most directly means the sample
options: was selected by random number generator
questions.explain: Bias occurs when the sampling process systematically over- or under-represents parts of the population.

questions.q: In stratified sampling the population is divided into groups and the number sampled from each group is
options: proportional to the size of the group
decided by who is easiest to reach
questions.explain: Stratified sampling takes a number from each stratum proportional to that stratum's size.

questions.q: What distinguishes a census from a sample?
options: A sample observes every member; a census observes only part
A census observes every member of the population; a sample observes only part of it
questions.explain: A census collects data from every member of the population, whereas a sample uses only a subset.

questions.q: Which is a disadvantage of opportunity sampling?
options: It requires a full numbered sampling frame
It is impossible to carry out quickly
It is extremely time-consuming to organise
It is very unlikely to be representative and can be highly biased
questions.explain: Opportunity sampling is convenient but tends to be unrepresentative and biased.

questions.q: Which statement about simple random sampling is a disadvantage?
options: It is biased by the interviewer
It requires a full list of the population, which may be hard to obtain
questions.explain: Simple random sampling needs a complete sampling frame, which can be impractical for large populations.

questions.q: Quota sampling is often chosen when
options: every population member must be surveyed
a complete sampling frame is available
no sampling frame exists and quick fieldwork is needed
questions.explain: Quota sampling is useful when no sampling frame exists and results are needed quickly and cheaply.

questions.q: Quota sampling differs from stratified sampling chiefly because
options: the interviewer selects members non-randomly until each quota is filled
it requires a complete sampling frame
the whole population must be surveyed
every member has an equal chance of selection
questions.explain: In quota sampling the interviewer non-randomly selects people to fill set quotas, without a random mechanism or sampling frame.

questions.q: A pilot survey is mainly used to
options: trial and refine the questions and methods before the main study
questions.explain: A pilot survey tests procedures and questions on a small scale before the full study.

questions.q: In simple random sampling, every
options: kth member is chosen after a random start
member has a different chance of selection
sample of the required size is equally likely to be chosen
group is sampled as a whole
questions.explain: In simple random sampling every possible sample of the given size is equally likely, so each member is equally likely to be selected.

questions.q: Non-response in a survey can introduce bias because
options: responders may differ systematically from non-responders
questions.explain: If those who do not respond differ from those who do, the achieved sample becomes biased.

questions.q: A school has 600 girls and 400 boys. In a stratified sample of 50, how many boys should be chosen?
questions.explain: Boys are 400 of 1000, so 400/1000 times 50 equals 20.

questions.q: Which method involves choosing members who are simply easiest to access?
questions.explain: Opportunity or convenience sampling takes whoever is available and easy to reach.

questions.q: A disadvantage of systematic sampling is that
options: it needs no ordering of the population
it is impossible to compute the interval
a periodic pattern in the list can coincide with the interval and cause bias
questions.explain: If the data has a cyclic pattern matching the sampling interval, systematic sampling can be biased.

questions.q: A town has 300 under-18s, 500 adults and 200 over-65s. A stratified sample of 100 should include how many adults?
questions.explain: Adults are 500 of 1000, so 500/1000 times 100 equals 50.
